\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{خطط} (khaṭṭaṭa)}{خطط (khaṭṭaṭa)}]{\ar{خطط} (khaṭṭaṭa) — to make plans}

\label{lesson:AR-C523-khattata}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for retired, then the Arabic for unemployed.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{خطط}}
\textbf{\ar{خطط}} — \emph{khaṭṭaṭa} — \textquotedblleft{}to make plans\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يخطط} \ar{أخي} \ar{لرحلة} \ar{في} \ar{الصيف}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yukhaṭṭiṭu akhī li-riḥla fī aṣ-ṣayf.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother is planning a trip in the summer.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يخطط}, \emph{yukhaṭṭiṭ}.

It takes \ar{لـ} for what is planned.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{خطط}} (\emph{khaṭṭaṭa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{kh-ṭ-ṭ}, \textquotedblleft{}to draw a line\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Khuṭṭa, a plan, which you know, is from the same root: a plan is lines drawn ahead.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khaṭṭaṭa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khaṭṭaṭa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yukhaṭṭiṭu akhī li-riḥla fī aṣ-ṣayf.} — My brother is planning a trip in the summer.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for retired, then the Arabic for unemployed, then say \emph{khaṭṭaṭa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{خطط} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To make plans\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أتم} (atamma)}{أتم (atamma)}]{\ar{أتم} (atamma) — to complete}

\label{lesson:AR-C523-atamma}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for unemployed, then the Arabic for to make plans.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أتم}}
\textbf{\ar{أتم}} — \emph{atamma} — \textquotedblleft{}to complete\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أتمت} \ar{أختي} \ar{دراستها} \ar{في} \ar{الجامعة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{atammat ukhtī dirāsatahā fī al-jāmiʿa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My sister completed her studies at the university.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتم}, \emph{yutimm}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أتم}} (\emph{atamma}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{t-m-m}, \textquotedblleft{}to be complete, whole\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Tamāman, completely, which you know, is from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تفرغ} (tafarragha)}{تفرغ (tafarragha)}]{\ar{تفرغ} (tafarragha) — to devote oneself}

\label{lesson:AR-C523-tafarragha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to make plans, then the Arabic for to complete.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تفرغ}}
\textbf{\ar{تفرغ}} — \emph{tafarragha} — \textquotedblleft{}to devote oneself\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تفرغ} \ar{أبي} \ar{لأسرته} \ar{بعد} \ar{التقاعد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tafarragha abī li-usratihi baʿda at-taqāʿud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father devoted himself to his family after he retired.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتفرغ}, \emph{yatafarragh}.

It takes \ar{لـ} for what you give your time to.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تفرغ}} (\emph{tafarragha}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{f-r-gh}, \textquotedblleft{}to be empty, free\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Fārigh, empty, which you know, is from the same root: Form V is to empty one's time for a thing.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tafarragha}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tafarragha abī li-usratihi baʿda at-taqāʿud.} — My father devoted himself to his family after he retired.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to make plans, then the Arabic for to complete, then say \emph{tafarragha} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تفرغ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To devote oneself\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تقييم} (taqyīm)}{تقييم (taqyīm)}]{\ar{تقييم} (taqyīm) — an evaluation, an assessment}

\label{lesson:AR-C523-taqyim}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to complete, then the Arabic for to devote oneself.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تقييم}}
\textbf{\ar{تقييم}} — \emph{taqyīm} — \textquotedblleft{}an evaluation, an assessment\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{حصل} \ar{الموظف} \ar{على} \ar{تقييم} \ar{ممتاز}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ḥaṣala al-muwaẓẓaf ʿalā taqyīm mumtāz.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The employee got an excellent evaluation.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تقييم}} (\emph{taqyīm}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{q-w-m}, \textquotedblleft{}to stand, to rise\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Qīma, value, is from the same root: taqyīm is fixing a thing's value.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taqyīm}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥaṣala al-muwaẓẓaf ʿalā taqyīm mumtāz.} — The employee got an excellent evaluation.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to complete, then the Arabic for to devote oneself, then say \emph{taqyīm} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{إنتاج} (intāj)}{إنتاج (intāj)}]{\ar{إنتاج} (intāj) — production}

\label{lesson:AR-C523-intaj}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to devote oneself, then the Arabic for an evaluation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{إنتاج}}
\textbf{\ar{إنتاج}} — \emph{intāj} — \textquotedblleft{}production\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{زاد} \ar{إنتاج} \ar{المصنع} \ar{هذه} \ar{السنة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{zāda intāj al-maṣnaʿ hādhihi as-sana.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The factory's production increased this year.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{إنتاج}} (\emph{intāj}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-t-j}, \textquotedblleft{}to bring forth young\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Intāj is the verbal noun of antaja, to produce.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{intāj}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zāda intāj al-maṣnaʿ hādhihi as-sana.} — The factory's production increased this year.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to devote oneself, then the Arabic for an evaluation, then say \emph{intāj} again
\end{itemize}
